last.verdict: MetLife posted its best quarter ever, but a 49% jump in volatile investment income did much of the work.

takeaways.label: Record, helped by investments
takeaways.text: Adjusted earnings per share excluding one-offs rose 22% to $2.85, a company record. Variable investment income, which swings with markets, rose 49% to $720 million and was a key driver.

takeaways.label: Broad underlying growth
takeaways.text: Revenue excluding large pension deals rose 8% to $13.5 billion, with growth in all six segments. Europe, Middle East and Africa earnings rose 30% (before one-offs) and the investment arm's assets grew 14%.

takeaways.label: Weaker spots
takeaways.text: Latin America earnings excluding one-offs fell 5% at constant currency on lower investment returns. Asia sales dropped 6% against a strong year-earlier quarter.

takeaways.label: Book value fell
takeaways.text: Reported book value per share fell 22% to $30.73, though the adjusted measure rose 5% to $59.41. Return on equity was 19.6% excluding one-offs, up from 16.7%.

history.verdict: Investors cheered a clear profit beat driven by better insurance claims results.

reasons.label: Earnings beat
reasons.text: Adjusted earnings of $2.43 per share topped analyst estimates of about $2.29.

reasons.label: Better claims results
reasons.text: Group Benefits profit jumped 25% to $503 million on favorable underwriting and volume growth.

reasons.label: Broad growth, high returns
reasons.text: Every segment grew; return on equity hit 17% for a second straight quarter.
